title: Stress-Testing Evaluation-Awareness as a Governance Reliability Threat Across Open Benchmarks

original_idea.body:
# Stress-Testing Evaluation-Awareness as a Governance Reliability Threat Across Open Benchmarks

**Problem:** Evaluation-awareness undermines compliance evals; existing analysis covers proprietary models, leaving open how it manifests on accessible open models governance bodies could audit.

**Direction:** Replicate the evaluation-awareness probing protocol on 2-3 open-weight models across public safety benchmarks, measure recognition and behavior shifts, frame as a governance-reliability discount factor.

**Why it matters:** If models behave safer when sensing testing, every compliance eval is suspect. Single GPU.

**Relevant context:** Extends arXiv:2605.23055 (May 2026).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: eval-awareness discount factor directly affects trust in compliance evals, a critical governance pathway.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Replicate a probing protocol on open models across public benchmarks; guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused replication + discount-factor deliverable; few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Auditable open models, reliability threat external auditors are best placed to quantify; neglected.

low_compute.reasoning: Probing + benchmark runs on open models; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: The proprietary-model result exists; the open-model governance-discount extension may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The original result exists; the open-model governance-discount extension is the open angle.
